newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Esso says minor Rotterdam refinery problem solved.
newsitem.headline: Esso says minor Rotterdam refinery problem solved.

text.p: Exxon Corp's Esso Netherlands said on Friday its Rotterdam refinery was running as normal after a small "hiccup" at its flexi-coker unit this morning.
"At the moment, there are no refinery problems at all," a spokesman said.
Earlier, traders said Esso was offering fuel oil at $110 fob ARA, some $5 below Thursday's closing level because of problems it faced restarting the unit.
Esso said the flexi-coker, down since mid-December, was restarted at the weekend. Traders earlier said cold conditions had scuppered Esso's attempts to restart the unit but the company denied this.
"(The restart) was successful. We had to take some extra precautions because of the cold, but that was it," the spokesman said.
"Essentially, we had a small hiccup (at the flexi-coker unit) this morning, but it is still operational... (The problem) is solved and (the unit) is running as normal," he said.
He did not give further details of the problem
When running normally, Esso's coker turns heavy fuel into light oil products at the rate of 7,000 tonnes a day, traders said.

A power outage in the Rotterdam area, in mid-December caused the closure of the entire 175,000 barrel per day refinery, but, apart from the flexi-coker, all other units were back in operation within 10 days.
